z-m-36-01.title: Two conditions that lead to the same place: what is their relationship to each other?
z-m-36-01.topic: What you can and cannot know when two conditions lead to the same condition (inclusion of truth sets)
z-m-36-01.goal: From only the information that 'if p then q' and 'if r then q' are true, sort out the statements that are settled and those that are not by the inclusion of truth sets, show the unsettled ones with counterexamples, and say what more you need to know to settle them.
z-m-36-01.material:
With the universal set U, consider three conditions p, q, r. Let their truth sets be P, Q, R. The only things you know are these two.
(가) The proposition 'if p then q' is true. (P is a subset of Q.)
(나) The proposition 'if r then q' is true. (R is a subset of Q.)
Nothing is known about the relationship between P and R. So that you can understand with words alone, without a picture, you can draw it as 'P is inside Q and R is also inside Q'.
z-m-36-01.thinking.0: Telling apart what is settled by the given information from what is 'not known'
z-m-36-01.thinking.1: Judging by turning conditions into inclusion of truth sets
z-m-36-01.thinking.2: Building counterexamples yourself to show 'not always true'
z-m-36-01.thinking.3: Saying what information is missing to settle a conclusion
z-m-36-01.prereq.0: That when the proposition 'if p then q' is true, the truth set P is a subset of Q, and that the contrapositive has the same truth value as the original proposition (assuming the learner has studied the first part of Common Mathematics 'sets and propositions'; H2 is only a difficulty label of this production assignment, not a grade designation)
z-m-36-01.prereq.1: The meaning of union, intersection and complement, and multiples and divisors
z-m-36-01.s.s1.prompt: Knowing only (가) and (나), choose all the statements that you can settle as always true. (Do not choose statements that cannot be settled.)
z-m-36-01.s.s1.hint.0: Draw two or more different pictures with P and R each placed inside Q. (For example, a picture where they overlap, and one where they do not overlap.)
z-m-36-01.s.s1.hint.1: Rewrite each statement as an inclusion such as 'P is a subset of Q' and check whether it is true in each picture you drew. Is there a statement whose truth changes depending on the picture?
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.a: All that is known is that P and R are both inside Q. Being inside the same set does not mean one includes the other. Also draw pictures where the two sets do not overlap or only one is large.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.b: If not q, then not p
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.b: You read (가) turned into its contrapositive. This judgment uses the fact that the contrapositive has the same truth value as the original proposition.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.c: This is the converse of (나). Even if a proposition is true, its converse can be true or false. Draw a picture where Q can be larger than R.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.d: If p or r, then q
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.d: This judgment checks whether the combined part of P and R fits inside Q. If each is inside Q, the combination is also inside Q.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.e: If p and r, then q
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.e: This judgment checks whether the common part of P and R fits inside Q. The common part is also part of P. Also think about the case where the common part is empty.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.o.f: If not r, then not p
z-m-36-01.s.s1.r.f: This statement is the contrapositive of 'if p then r'. If that statement is not settled, this one is not settled either.
z-m-36-01.s.s1.explain: What is settled from (가) and (나) is only what follows directly from P⊂Q and R⊂Q. 'If not q, then not p' is the contrapositive of (가), 'if p or r, then q' is P∪R⊂Q, and 'if p and r, then q' is P∩R⊂Q. On the other hand, 'if p, then r' (P⊂R) and its contrapositive, and 'if q, then r' (Q⊂R), can be true or false depending on how P, R, and Q are placed, so they are not settled by this information alone. 'Not settled' is different from 'false'.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.prompt: Now let's look at a concrete case. The universal set U is the natural numbers from 1 to 30. q is 'is even', p is 'is a multiple of 4', and r is 'is a multiple of 6'. Then (가) and (나) are both true. Find and enter 3 different numbers x for which p is true but r is false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.hint.0: First list all the numbers from 1 to 30 that satisfy the condition p (multiples of 4).
z-m-36-01.s.s2.hint.1: For each number you listed, check the condition r (whether it is a multiple of 6), and keep only the numbers that do not satisfy it.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.ok.c1: It is a natural number from 1 to 30.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c1: x must be a natural number from 1 to 30.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.ok.c2: It is a multiple of 4, so p is true.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c2: It is not a multiple of 4, so p is not true.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.ok.c3: It is not a multiple of 6, so r is false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.fail.c3: It is a multiple of 6, so r is true. It has to be a number for which r is false.
z-m-36-01.s.s2.explain: From 1 to 30, the multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, and removing 12 and 24, which are multiples of 6, leaves 4, 8, 16, 20, 28, which fit the condition. If there is even one such number, 'if p then r' is false. Even in this case (가) and (나) are still true, so it is confirmed that (가) and (나) alone cannot settle 'if p then r'.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.prompt: Jiho said, "p and r are both inside q, so 'if p then r' must be true too." Write what you think about Jiho's statement. Also write whether what I first chose in s1 changed (or stayed the same) after doing s2, and write what more information is needed to settle that 'if p then r' is true.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.hint.0: Pick one of the numbers you made in s2 and first write whether p and r are each true or false.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.hint.1: Think about what shape one more statement directly connecting p and r would take, and check whether the number you just chose is still possible when that statement exists.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.placeholder: Example: Jiho's statement is ... because ... To settle it ...
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.0: In the number I gave, can you clearly see that p is true and r is false?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.1: Did I write 'cannot be settled' and 'is false' as different things?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.2: If the additional information I mentioned existed, did I check with one example that 'if p then r' really becomes true?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.selfAssess.3: If what I first chose in s1 changed, did I write why it changed, and if it stayed the same, on what grounds?
z-m-36-01.s.s3.model.0: Jiho's statement can't be settled. 4 is a multiple of 4, so p is true, but it is not a multiple of 6, so r is false. Still (가) and (나) stay true, so being inside q alone is not enough. We need something more that directly connects p and r, like the information that P is inside R.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.modelNote.0: If you did not choose 'if p then r' at first, it is a case where your judgment stayed the same, and you can write that checking with an example made your confidence grow.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.model.1: I can't tell if it is true. 16 is a multiple of 4 but not a multiple of 6, so it is a counterexample. But if we also learn 'if q then r', then P is inside Q and Q is inside R, so P is inside R too, and 'if p then r' becomes true. At first it seemed likely to be true, but I found a counterexample and changed my mind.
z-m-36-01.s.s3.modelNote.1: An answer that gives one piece of new information and also says why it is enough. The case R=Q becomes 'if q then r' when combined with (나), so it is another way of saying the same answer.
